transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because I’ve just been worrying a lot—probably more than I should. It feels like it’s all kind of happening at once: my marriage, work and whether I’m falling behind there, bills, stuff around the house I keep not finishing… and I keep getting stuck on this thought that I’m not doing well enough as a husband or a dad. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been hard to turn off.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of life, rather than mainly one specific problem?

Yeah… I think it’s more than one thing. I wish I could say it was just one specific problem, but it sort of jumps around—or really, it’s all of it at once. My marriage, work and whether I’m slipping there, bills, projects around the house I keep dropping… and then I start wondering if I’m just not doing enough as a husband or a dad.  

I don’t know if that makes sense, but yeah, it’s not just one issue.
How long have you been worrying like this?

I think… probably around nine months? I mean, it wasn’t like one day it suddenly started, but that’s when it became hard to ignore. Around when the cloud migration at work really ramped up, and arguments at home started happening more regularly.  

So, yeah… about nine months, if that’s helpful.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yeah… I mean, I try to stop it. I’ll tell myself, “Just focus on the code in front of you,” or if I’m working out I’ll try to just breathe and get through that, and sometimes it helps for a minute.

But honestly, a lot of the time one worry kind of grabs onto the next one. Like I’ll start with something small at work, and pretty quickly I’m imagining a bad review, then losing my job, then my family being worse off because of me. I know that sounds dramatic… I’m not trying to overstate it. It just gets ahead of me before I can really shut it down.
Do you find yourself doing any repetitive behaviors or mental rituals to try to relieve these worries?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in the way I imagine you mean, like checking the stove ten times or having to do things in a certain order.

I mean, I’ll sometimes go over things in my head a lot, but that feels more like… worrying, I guess, not a ritual. I don’t think I have any specific repetitive thing I do to make it go away. Does that answer it okay?
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try not to make a big deal of it, but I feel kind of wound tight most of the day.

My shoulders are usually locked up, like I’m bracing for something even when nothing is actually happening. And I notice I’ll pace between meetings, or if I’m at chess club I’m tapping pieces without really meaning to. Sitting still just feels… harder than it should, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed كثيرًا lately?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean… I have moments where I feel kind of worn down or discouraged, but I don’t want to overstate it.

Lately it’s more like I get tired of feeling on edge, if that makes sense. But “down a lot” — I don’t know. Maybe a little sometimes, but I wouldn’t say that’s the main thing. Is that answering what you mean?
Do these worries feel mainly like a reaction to the problems at work and at home, or do they feel broader than that?

I think… broader, honestly. I mean, work and home are definitely part of it, but it doesn’t stay in one lane.

It’s like I start worrying about my marriage, then whether I’m slipping at work, then bills, then stuff around the house I haven’t finished… and then it turns into this bigger feeling like I’m just failing as a husband and a father. I know that probably sounds dramatic, and I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, but it feels like everything at once sometimes.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah… a bit. I mean, I do sleep, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m up all night every night, but most nights I get into bed exhausted and then my mind just won’t shut off.

It’ll start going through work stuff, money, things I said to my wife… like replaying or trying to fix things in my head. And then if I do fall asleep, I’ll wake up around 3 or 4, and it’s like I’m already thinking through tomorrow’s problems before I’m even fully awake. Then getting back to sleep is really hard. Is that the kind of trouble sleeping you mean?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… I guess I have, more than I’d like to admit. I still get things done, so I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function, but it’s harder.

Like during sprint planning or code reviews, I’ll read the same design note three or four times and then realize I still missed something obvious. Part of my brain is supposed to be on the code, but another part is off thinking about what I forgot to do at home, or how the next argument is going to go.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I’m trying to pay attention, but I keep having to pull myself back. Does that count as trouble concentrating?
During the past two weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day?

I… don’t think I’d say most of the day nearly every day. I mean, I’ve had some low moments, sure, but “depressed or hopeless” sounds… I don’t know, stronger than what I’d want to claim.

Mostly I feel worn down and worried, if that makes sense. But not like I’m sad all day every day. Is that the distinction you’re asking about?
Did these worries begin after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Yeah… I think there was a kind of starting point. Not one single dramatic event exactly, but around nine months ago the cloud migration at work really ramped up, and around the same time the arguments at home started becoming more regular.

I don’t want to make it sound like everything fell apart overnight, because it didn’t, but that’s when the worrying started to feel more constant. Does that answer what you mean by after a specific change?
Are you still going through the work and marriage problems that seemed to start this, or have those stressors already ended?

They’re… still going on, yeah. I wish I could say they’d settled down, but they haven’t really.

Work is still pretty intense, and I’m trying to keep up, but my manager has started writing down missed architectural details in a way that feels more formal than before. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m failing at my job, but it’s definitely being noticed.

And at home, the marriage stuff hasn’t really resolved either. I’ll start things around the house and leave them half-finished, or I’m physically there but distracted, and then that becomes part of the argument too. So… yes, I think the stressors are still active. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do the amount and intensity of your worry feel out of proportion to what’s actually going on in your life?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I can list reasons that make the worry sound legitimate—my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, the house stuff I keep starting and then dropping—but the amount of space it takes up in my head feels bigger than the actual problems sometimes.

It’s like I can’t stop worrying about everything at once, and then it turns into this bigger question of whether I’m basically failing as a husband and father. I know that may sound dramatic, and I’m not trying to overstate it, but… yes, the intensity feels out of proportion.
Have these worries been interfering with your work or your responsibilities at home?

Yes… I think it has, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

At work, my manager has started documenting some missed architectural details, which is embarrassing to say. It’s not like I’m not trying, but things are slipping enough that it’s being noticed.

And at home, yeah… I’ll start projects and not finish them, or I’m there but distracted, and then that turns into more arguments. So I guess the honest answer is yes, it’s interfering. Is that the kind of impact you’re asking about?
Even when nothing stressful is happening in the moment, do you still find yourself feeling anxious or worrying?

Yeah… unfortunately, yes. Even when nothing is actually happening right then, my mind kind of keeps going.

I’ll be sitting there and it’s like everything lines up at once—my marriage, work, bills, stuff around the house I haven’t finished—and then it turns into this bigger worry that I’m failing as a husband or father. I know that sounds… maybe a little excessive, but that’s honestly why I came in. I just can’t seem to shut it off.
